sections.title: What is Local Python (Embeddable Runtime)?
sections.content:
The Local Python tab is used for downloading and managing 'Windows Embeddable' Python versions. These are official, lightweight package distributions directly from python.org.

Why use them instead of a standard installation?

  • Absolute Isolation: These versions are not installed into Windows. They do not write to the system registry and do not modify system environment variables (PATH).
  • Portability: When creating a virtual environment (venv) from Local Python, the entire structure is portable. You can copy it to a USB drive and it will work on any other computer.
  • Multi-version Testing: You can have Python 3.9, 3.10, and 3.13 downloaded side-by-side without them conflicting on your system.

sections.title: Installation and Sources (URL/ZIP)
sections.content:
At the top of the tab, you can add a new Python version to the application. You have three options:

  1. Selection from default list: In the dropdown menu, you will find pre-configured secure download links for the most popular versions directly from Python servers.
  2. Custom URL: If your desired version is missing from the list, paste a direct link to the .zip file (must start with http/https and end with .zip).
  3. Local ZIP file: If you already have a Python .zip downloaded on your PC, click the folder icon 📁 and select it. The application will not download it, only extract it.

Installation Process and Permissions

Where Python is installed depends on your setup mode:

  • In Classic Installation: The default path is the shared folder C:\ProgramData\VenvHubPro\PyRuntimes. This folder is shared across all PC users, preventing data duplication.
  • In Portable Mode: It is stored directly in the PyRuntimes folder next to the application, preserving 100% portability on a USB drive.
Seamless Operation Without UAC: The setup wizard automatically configured folder permissions during installation (using the system command icacls for the Users group) for the ProgramData\VenvHubPro directory. This means downloading, extracting, and managing local Python versions runs seamlessly in the background without requiring administrator (UAC) privileges in daily use.

sections.title: Critical Step: Fixing PIP (Must-do!)
sections.content:
Once the new version is installed and appears in the 'Installed runtimes' table, you will notice that the 'PIP Status' column displays a red ❌ Missing.

Reason: The lightweight 'Embeddable' Python builds from python.org developers are intentionally stripped down. By default, they lack the package installer (Pip) and have disabled access to third-party libraries (site-packages).

What do you need to do?

Click the corresponding row in the table and press the ✅ Fix PIP button. VenvHub Pro will then perform a series of essential adjustments and patches:

  1. Downloads Bootstrap: The application silently downloads the official get-pip.py script.
  2. Unlocks Site Isolation (._pth file): VenvHub Pro locates the internal configuration file inside Python (e.g. python313._pth) and programmatically uncomments the line import site. Without this step, Python would ignore any packages installed into it.
  3. Installs PIP and Virtualenv: The script executes, installs Pip, and subsequently downloads the virtualenv package. (Embeddable distributions do not include the standard venv module for environment creation, which VenvHub replaces with the more powerful virtualenv tool).
Result: Upon completion, the status in the table changes to ✅ OK. From this point forward, this runtime behaves as a fully-featured, high-performance, and portable Python installation ready for creating environments in the main Manager.

sections.title: Customizing the Version List (JSONL)
sections.content:
The version list in the dropdown menu is not hardcoded into the application. It is loaded dynamically from the text file jso_python_ver.jsonl in the assets folder. When a new Python release comes out, you can add it to the list yourself.

  1. Click the ✏️ Edit List button.
  2. The application opens the file in Notepad. (Note: If the application is located in Program Files, Notepad will prompt for administrator privileges via UAC).
  3. Add a new line using this exact format:
    {"name": "Python 3.14.0", "url": "https://link-to-zip-file.zip"}
  4. Save the file (Ctrl+S) and close Notepad.

VenvHub Pro utilizes the QFileSystemWatcher module to actively monitor changes in this file. As soon as you save it, the dropdown menu in the application synchronizes immediately without requiring a restart.

sections.title: Management, Deletion, and Cache Memory
sections.content:
Performance via Cache Memory

To avoid UI lag and slow load times, VenvHub Pro does not read the list of installed Python versions and their statuses from the disk every time you switch tabs. It stores them in fast runtime memory (RAM).

How to Properly Delete Python Versions?

Because the application relies on cache memory, never delete Python directories manually via Windows Explorer! The application would remain unaware of the change, the version would still appear in the table, and attempting to use it would result in errors.

  • Always use the ❌ Delete button directly in the application. VenvHub Pro will safely remove all files from disk and instantly clear the entry from its internal memory.

What if the table becomes desynchronized? (Refresh Button)

If you deleted a folder manually despite the warning, or added one by copying it from another PC, click the 🔄 (Refresh) button below the table.

This forces a 'Hard Refresh'. The application invalidates its cache, physically rescans the disk, and re-evaluates all detected Python runtimes, syncing the table with the actual disk state.
